reason: Both plans satisfy the hard requirements (phased rollout with percentages/entry criteria, well-formatted risks, numeric halt thresholds, and no decommissioning in the same phase as final migration), but Response A is more rigorous and professional overall—it adds a dedicated pre-migration readiness phase, more precisely defined halt metrics (exact discrepancy formula, percentage-point deltas), and more detailed enterprise/rollback handling. Response B is comparable in structure but includes an unprofessional 'May the Force be with you' aside that has no place in a business rollout document, slightly undercutting its usefulness as a deliverable.
